lines.text: Second hour of my night. I've not seen this town in daylight since the spring.
Third hour nothing, fourth hour nothing. What goes in the margin is mostly Wispurr, and they're up once the cold comes.
Fourteen in a night last winter and not one since the thaw, so the page has stayed empty.
Whatever Bly told you. A jar and a half left, second week of the month.
Same three rooms, same two lamps, and I am buying oil now at a rate I never used to. The lampwright wants what he wanted in the spring and I have told him so to his face.

There was a wick in my hand when you came through that door and there is a wick in it still. I trim my own. The week is not out yet, so I could not tell you what it has cost me even if you asked me to.
My shutters are open all night and my lamp's out. So if I get a Wispurr I'm keeping it in the shed. That's settled.
It has to be winter, she says, and winter takes forever, it's been nearly a week already.
So you'll say it to her when you're passing. I'll leave the shed door on the latch. Then it's done and nobody has to keep on about it.
Cold-pressed, then strained, then strained again through flannel. Four burns to the fill.

I would stand on four. Anything giving you less was strained the once and jarred while the oil was still warm, and you can taste that on the second burn. The wick gauge matters more than the oil does anyway.
Fourteen to the inch. Any finer will not draw and any coarser smokes.
The ground's thin up the vale and dark half the day. The flock does very well on it.
The lambs are carrying weight this year and you can put a hand on one and feel it. So.

Umbrat graze that ground alongside my sheep. The Wispurr come hunting the Umbrat once the cold's in, and neither has ever had a lamb off me. The dogs and I go up past the Sanctum gate of a morning and come down at dusk.
Stand off the east side while I'm reading. Town's lamps in the glass again.
I am out here rather than in the town because in the town the lamps sit in the glass all night.
The vale goes dark at about a degree a decade. The chart carries the rate and it carries no reason for it.
My figure for the day is nought. Company scout, posted here at first light to write down what comes back down.
The approach took six teams at first light and it is past noon.
Written out longhand. n, o, u, g, h, t. The gate was already open when we got here. The people I report to would not want that said out loud. I've gone and said it anyway. I am going to stop now.
